originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus queries, accessible historical claims and primary full scientific texts were compared by equivalence and implication. The closest open-neighborhood theorem has a different simplicial complex and no H2; the classical girth statement excludes squares, while Cartesian-product and hypercube results cover restricted proper subclasses. No equivalent arbitrary graph classification or natural signed square-module was found; unindexed stronger coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: A stronger unindexed result on closed-neighborhood graph Čech complexes with edge-disjoint four-cycles could exist.
Metric gluing results on special classes can imply some individual cactus cases but have not been shown to cover all noncactus edge-disjoint-square graphs.
Same-source public revisions after the inspected versions could change priority.

value.rationale: A natural infinite graph class localizes the failure of the high-girth Čech reconstruction regime. The full homotopy classification identifies one independent H2 sphere generated by every square, the precise loss in H1, the free fundamental group, and the signed automorphism action; the result extends beyond cactus graphs to graphs with retained longer cycles and provides a structural tool, not a routine parameter increment.
